s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly enlarging, tender mass in the buttock with recent onset of constipation and numbness in the lower extremity
salient_findings: Tender, palpable mass in the left buttock
Numbness of the left lower extremity worsened by sitting
Hypoesthesia in the L5-S4 distribution on the left
key_facts: 21-year-old man with no past medical or surgical history
Mass in the left buttock noticed for several years, rapidly enlarged over six months
No drainage, redness, fever, or systemic symptoms
No medications or family history of cancer
4 × 4 cm tender mass in the left perineum without overlying skin changes
Intact motor function in the left lower extremity
Abdominal and digital rectal examinations were unremarkable
Contrast-enhanced CT of the pelvis showed a well-defined, nonenhancing, unilocular hypodense cystic lesion
Contrast-enhanced MRI showed homogeneous, T1 hypointense, T2 hyperintense lesions with no wall enhancement

shortlist.label: Tarlov cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a well-defined, nonenhancing, unilocular hypodense cystic lesion, are consistent with a Tarlov cyst, which is a type of cyst that can occur in the spine and pelvis

shortlist.label: Pilonidal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The location of the mass in the left buttock and the patient's symptoms, such as tenderness and numbness, could be consistent with a pilonidal cyst, although the imaging findings are not typical

shortlist.label: Perineal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a cystic lesion in the perineum, could be consistent with a perineal cyst, which is a type of cyst that can occur in the perineal region

shortlist.label: Pudendal nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms, such as numbness and tenderness, could be consistent with a schwannoma of the pudendal nerve, which is a type of nerve tumor that can occur in the pelvis

shortlist.label: Ganglion cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a well-defined, nonenhancing, unilocular hypodense cystic lesion, could be consistent with a ganglion cyst, which is a type of cyst that can occur in the soft tissues

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a tender, palpable mass in the left buttock with recent onset of constipation and numbness of the left lower extremity, along with imaging findings of a well-defined, nonenhancing, unilocular hypodense cystic lesion, is consistent with a Tarlov cyst, which is a type of cyst that occurs in the spinal canal and can compress nearby nerves, leading to neurological symptoms.

rejected.label: Pilonidal cyst
rejected.why: Pilonidal cysts typically present with drainage, redness, and fever, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Perineal cyst
rejected.why: Perineal cysts are not typically associated with the neurological symptoms described in this case.

rejected.label: Pudendal nerve schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically solid tumors, whereas the imaging findings in this case show a cystic lesion.

rejected.label: Ganglion cyst
rejected.why: Ganglion cysts are typically found in the wrist or hand and are not typically associated with the symptoms or imaging findings described in this case.
